key_insight: A Bayesian-optimization plus discrete biorthogonal wavelet approach can rapidly find and robustly identify the correct laser frequency reference for auto-locking.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable field-deployable laser stabilization for quantum communications, quantum computing, and precision measurement systems.
method: Use Bayesian optimization to guide reference searching from prior observations instead of blind parameter scans.
Apply discrete biorthogonal wavelet transformation to detect transition signals and extract invariant frequency differences and relative magnitudes.
Close the loop with a lead zirconate titanate-current double-servo lock to stabilize the laser frequency.
evidence_signal: The method reportedly achieves 5× faster reference searching, >99.5% identification accuracy under strong perturbations, and a locked linewidth of 20 kHz.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurate wavelet feature extraction and system-specific calibration when transferring to different atoms, optics, or noise conditions.
paper_title: Rapid and robust laser-frequency auto-locking using Bayesian-optimization and discrete-wavelet-transformation algorithms
